name: VWAP Distance In ATRs
pine:
//@version=5
indicator("VWAP Distance In ATRs", shorttitle="VWAP-ATR", overlay=false)

period = input.int(14, "ATR Length", minval=1)
band   = input.float(1.0, "Band (ATRs)", minval=0.0, step=0.25)

vw  = ta.vwap(hlc3)
atrv = ta.atr(period)

osc = atrv > 0 ? (close - vw) / atrv : na

plot(osc, title="VWAP-ATR", color=color.new(color.blue, 0), linewidth=2)
hline(0, "VWAP", color=color.gray, linestyle=hline.style_solid)
ub = plot(band, title="Upper", color=color.new(color.gray, 50))
lb = plot(-band, title="Lower", color=color.new(color.gray, 50))
fill(ub, lb, color=color.new(color.gray, 92), title="Band")

alertcondition(ta.crossover(osc, 0),  title="Crossed above VWAP", message="Price crossed above session VWAP")
alertcondition(ta.crossunder(osc, 0), title="Crossed below VWAP", message="Price crossed below session VWAP")
note: Plots how far the close sits above or below the session VWAP in units of ATR, so it crosses zero exactly at VWAP and the ±1 band marks a one-ATR stretch that is comparable across symbols and volatility regimes.
warning: VWAP resets at each new b.day and is volume-weighted on hlc3 (falling back to an unweighted typical-price average only if that session's volume is zero or missing), while the ATR is Wilder's and runs continuously across sessions rather than resetting — a daily reset would make the first bars of each day divide by an almost-undefined range. Consequence: the first bar of every session reads ~0 by construction, since VWAP equals that bar's typical price. On daily or higher bars each bar is its own session, so the output is near-zero noise; this is an intraday indicator.
prompt: Distance from the session VWAP measured in ATRs, as an oscillator that crosses zero at VWAP
